STUDY TIP:
Don't just read for knowledge, read for transformation. Ask: What does this say? What does it mean to me? What will I do today? Reading the Bible is not like reading a normal book for school. Many people read to finish chapters, to get knowledge, to be able to quote verses, but God did not give us His Word just for information, He gave it for transformation. The goal is not to know about the Bible, but to let the Bible change you. Every time you open your Bible as a youth, don't rush. Pause and pray first. Say, "Holy Spirit, teach me. Show me Jesus today."
Then apply the 3 questions:
 1. What does this say? (Observation) - What is really happening in this verse? Who is speaking? Who is listening? What is the context? Don't just read one verse alone, read the verse before and after. For example, when you read "I can do all things through Christ" in Philippians 4:13, what does it really say? Paul was in prison, lacking food and comfort, yet he was learning contentment in Christ. It's not just about passing exams, it's about strength to endure any season.
2. What does it mean to me? (Interpretation) - How does this connect to my life as a young Christian in 2026? What does this reveal about God? What does it reveal about me? Does it show me a sin to confess? A promise to claim? An example to follow? A command to obey? If God says "Don't let anyone look down on you because you are young" in 1 Timothy 4:12, it means your youth is not a weakness, it is your weapon. God wants to use you NOW, not when you are old.
3. What will I do today? (Application) - This is where transformation happens. Knowledge without action makes you proud, but knowledge with action makes you grow. Write down one practical thing you will DO today because of what you read. Not tomorrow, today. Maybe you need to forgive someone, delete something from your phone, start praying for 10 minutes in the morning, or share the verse with a friend. Faith without action is dead.
Practical tips for you: Keep a small notebook or use your phone's notes. Write Date, Verse, What God told me, What I will do. Keep your fire burning daily like Leviticus 6:13 says - "The fire shall ever be burning upon the altar; it shall never go out." Your personal altar is your daily quiet time. Even 15 minutes every day is better than 2 hours once a week. Be consistent. Use YouTube tutorials, but don't replace reading yourself. Let the Word wash your mind. Don't just scroll TikTok and then quickly read one verse to feel better. Give God your best time, not your leftover time. And finally, study with others. Share what you learned in your youth group, on Faith Connect. When you teach what you learned, you remember it forever.
-Remember, the Bible is not a book to finish, it is a life to live.
